transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... it's my head. My mind just keeps going blank at the absolute worst times. Like, I'll be at work, and I'll look at the road-closure forms or even just holding my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I cannot remember the steps. And I've done this for years. It's like the time just evaporates. Which reminds me, the other day, this guy in a blue Honda—he had this bumper sticker about saving the bees, which I think is so important because, you know, without bees, the whole ecosystem just collapses. I watched this documentary once about how they communicate through dancing, and it just makes you wonder how much we don't understand about insects. But anyway, yeah, I just stand there holding the sign and my brain is just... empty.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized or high compared with your normal self?

Energized? No... no, I don't think so. Honestly, most of the time I just feel incredibly heavy. Like I'm walking through wet cement. I do try to drink coffee to get some kind of energy for my shifts, though. There's this little drive-thru espresso hut right by the intersection where I'm flagging this week, and the girl working there makes the best mochas. She actually brings her dog to work, this little terrier mix, and it just sits on the counter by the window. 

I always worry about the dog, honestly, because of all the cars idling right there in line. The exhaust can't be good for its little lungs. I read an article once about air quality and how it affects pets faster than humans because they breathe faster... or maybe it's because they're closer to the ground? I can't remember. My mom used to have a dog that had asthma, and they had to give it an inhaler, which just seems so strange to look at. 

But anyway... no. I never really get those big bursts of energy or feel high like you're saying. I'm usually just tired.
When you were a child in school, did you often have trouble paying attention?

Trouble paying attention in school? I... I don't really remember having a problem with it. I was pretty quiet, mostly. I liked reading. I remember reading this one book about a girl who lived in a windmill, and she had to figure out how to grind the flour herself after her parents left. It was so detailed about the gears and the stones. I actually tried to build a little model windmill out of popsicle sticks and rubber bands for a science project after that. My dad helped me glue the base together because the glue gun was so hot. He used to keep all his tools in these old metal coffee cans in the garage, the kind that smelled like stale coffee and motor oil. He had this whole system for sorting the nails by size, but then my brother knocked one over once and they just went everywhere. It took us hours to pick them all up out of the sawdust on the floor. 

But no, I don't think I had trouble paying attention. I just kind of kept my head down and did my work.
When your mind goes blank, do you lose track of time?

Lose track of time? Um... yeah, I guess I do. It's like... I'll look at the clock on my phone, and it's 10:15, and then I blink, and my supervisor is tapping me on the shoulder to tell me it's time for my lunch break at noon. My phone actually has this really annoying crack right across the screen, right where the time is. I dropped it last week when I was trying to get my keys out of my pocket. My keychain is so heavy because I have all these little charms on it. There's a little Eiffel Tower from when my aunt went to Paris, and this plastic dinosaur that glows in the dark. I think it's a Stegosaurus, the one with the plates on its back. Did you know they think those plates were actually for regulating their body temperature, not just for defense? I read that in a waiting room magazine once. It's fascinating how much we've learned about dinosaurs just from fossils. They even found one recently that had preserved feathers, which completely changes how you picture them. It makes them seem more like giant, scary birds. 

But, um... yeah, the time just kind of vanishes when my head gets empty like that. I just don't know where it goes.
During these blank spells, are you aware of what’s happening around you?

Aware? I... I don't think so. That's actually why I came in, to be honest. It's getting really bad at work. I'll be standing there, and I'll look down at the road-closure forms I have to sign, or even just holding my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just... I cannot remember the steps. And I've done this job for years. But my mind just goes completely blank at the worst possible times. 

Like the other day, I was standing by the barricades, and they're those big orange plastic ones, you know? The ones you can fill with water or sand so they don't blow over. The crew usually fills them with water from the hydrant, which always makes me nervous because the water pressure from those things is incredible. I saw a video once where a fire hydrant broke and the water shot up higher than a three-story building. It completely flooded the street in like five minutes. Water damage is so hard to fix, too. My sister had a pipe burst in her basement last winter, and it ruined all her old photo albums. She had these beautiful leather-bound albums from our grandparents' wedding, and they just got completely soaked and warped. She tried to dry them out with a hair dryer, but the pages all stuck together. It was really heartbreaking.

But... yeah, when the blankness happens, I'm just gone. I don't know what's happening around me at all until I snap out of it and realize I don't know what I'm supposed to be doing with the paddle.
After one of these blank spells ends, can you remember what happened during it?

Remember what happened? No, not really. It's just a blank. Like I was saying, that's the whole reason I'm here. It's just so terrifying to be holding the stop-slow paddle, or staring at those road-closure forms, and I just completely forget the steps. Things I've done for years. It's like someone just hit erase. 

You know, those forms are always printed on this really cheap, thin paper that tears if you even look at it wrong. The ink smears, too, especially when it rains. We have to use these special waterproof clipboards, the ones that have a little plastic cover that folds down over the paper. My supervisor, Dave, he lost his clipboard last month and had to use a regular one during a downpour. The forms practically dissolved. Dave is always losing things, though. He lost his favorite sunglasses in a porta-potty once. He was so mad because they were those expensive polarized ones that cut the glare off the windshields. Glare can be really dangerous out on the road, especially right at sunrise or sunset. The light hits the asphalt and it just blinds you. 

But yeah, I don't remember anything from when it happens. Just... gone. And then I'm standing there holding the paddle like an idiot.
Do these blank spells tend to happen when you’re under emotional stress?

Emotional stress? I mean... maybe? I'm not really sure if it's stress causing it, but like I said, it just happens at the absolute worst times. I'll just be standing there, looking at the road-closure forms or holding my stop-slow paddle, and my mind just completely empties out. I suddenly cannot remember the steps for things I've done for years. It's so frustrating. 

Speaking of those road-closure forms, they changed the font on them recently. It used to be Arial, I think, but now it's something with those little feet on the letters... serifs, right? It makes it look so much more formal, almost like a legal document you'd get from a lawyer. My cousin is a lawyer, actually. She works in corporate law downtown. She has this amazing office on the thirtieth floor with floor-to-ceiling windows. You can see the whole city from up there. She says it's terrifying during thunderstorms, though, because the building actually sways a little bit in the wind. I don't think I could handle that. I get motion sickness just riding in the backseat of a car. I have to chew ginger gum whenever I take a cab. Ginger is supposed to be really good for your digestion, too. I buy these little crystallized ginger pieces from the health food store, but they're so spicy sometimes they make my eyes water. 

But, um... yeah, my mind just goes blank. I don't know if it's stress, but it's why I'm here. I just look at the paddle and I don't know what to do with it.
Has anyone ever told you that you shake or have jerking movements during one of these blank spells?

Shake or jerk? No, no one's ever said anything like that to me. I think I just stand there, completely still. Like a statue. Which is why I'm so worried about work, because if I'm just standing there frozen with the stop-slow paddle, someone could get hurt. I just... I forget the steps. 

I did see a statue once that looked incredibly real. It was one of those living statue street performers down by the harbor. He was painted completely bronze, head to toe, and he stood on this little milk crate for hours without blinking. I don't know how they do that without getting muscle cramps. I get a charley horse in my calf almost every night. My doctor told me to eat more bananas for the potassium, but I really can't stand the texture of bananas. They're just so mushy. I prefer apples, especially the Honeycrisp ones when they're in season. They're so expensive, though. I saw them for almost four dollars a pound at the grocery store last week. The prices of everything are just going up so fast. A carton of eggs is ridiculous now. 

But no, nobody has ever told me I shake or anything. I just... freeze up and my mind goes totally blank.
Right before one of these blank spells starts, do you suddenly feel a wave of intense fear or panic?

Fear or panic? Um... no, I don't think so. I don't feel anything coming on. It's just... one second I'm there, holding the paddle or looking at the forms, and the next second it's just blank. I don't get any kind of warning like that. 

Speaking of warnings, though, we have these new early warning signs for the work zones. They have these really bright, flashing LED lights on them now. They're supposed to be solar-powered, which is great for the environment, you know? I try to do my part, I recycle all my plastics and cardboard. Although, the recycling rules in my neighborhood keep changing. One week you can put glass in the blue bin, the next week you have to take it to a special drop-off center. The drop-off center is right next to this amazing little bakery, though. They make these blueberry scones that are just incredible. They put a lemon glaze on top that perfectly balances out the sweetness. I tried to bake scones at home once, but they turned out hard as rocks. I think my baking powder was expired. You really have to check the expiration dates on things. I drank some milk once that was a week past the date, and my stomach was upset for two whole days. 

But no, I don't feel any panic or fear right before it happens. It just... happens, and then I'm standing there, totally lost.
Has anyone ever seen you do repetitive movements, like lip smacking or picking at things, during one of these blank spells?

Lip smacking? No, I don't think so. None of the other flaggers have ever mentioned me doing anything weird like that. Although, my lips do get incredibly chapped out there on the road with all the wind and the dust from the construction. I have to carry this special beeswax lip balm in my safety vest pocket all the time. It has peppermint in it, which is supposed to be really soothing. Peppermint is great for headaches, too, you know. My aunt used to grow real peppermint in her garden. She had this massive garden in her backyard with all these wooden raised beds. She grew tomatoes that were the size of softballs, I swear. We used to make fresh salsa every single summer. I love a good salsa, but it absolutely has to have cilantro in it. Some people think cilantro tastes like soap, which I read somewhere is actually a genetic thing. I think genetics are so fascinating. Like how my sister and I both have the exact same freckle on our left wrist, right over the vein. 

But, um... what was it? Picking at things? No. Nobody has ever said I do anything like that when my mind empties out. I really think I just stand there frozen.
Have you ever had a head injury?

A head injury? No, I've never hit my head or been knocked out or anything like that. I've always been pretty careful. Even when I was a kid, I was the one who wouldn't ride my bike without a helmet. My mom bought me this bright pink helmet with little white stars on it. It was so ugly, but she made me wear it. 

I see kids riding around now without helmets all the time, and it just makes me so nervous. Especially with the way people drive these days. People are always looking at their phones while they're driving. Just yesterday, I was holding the stop sign, and this guy in a silver sedan drove right past me because he was texting. He didn't even look up! I had to blow my whistle so hard I thought I was going to burst an eardrum. Whistles are surprisingly loud when you blow them with all your might. I actually have a special whistle that's designed to cut through the noise of heavy machinery. It's made of this lightweight titanium, so it doesn't weigh down my lanyard. Lanyards can really chafe your neck if you wear them all day in the heat. I tried wrapping mine in a bit of felt, but then it just absorbed all my sweat and got really gross. 

But no, I've never had a concussion or hurt my head. My head is totally fine, except for... well, the blank spells.
Have you ever been told that you have seizures or epilepsy?

Seizures? No, nobody's ever told me that. I've never had a seizure or epilepsy or anything. My health has always been pretty normal, honestly. Except for my allergies, I guess. I have terrible seasonal allergies, especially in the spring when all the pollen is out. The oak trees are the worst for me. There's this massive oak tree right outside my bedroom window, and it just dumps yellow dust all over my car every April. I have to run it through the car wash like twice a week just to see out the windshield. The car wash I go to has those really cool colorful foam soaps, you know? Like bright pink and blue. It smells like bubblegum. I used to love bubblegum when I was little, especially the kind that came in a long tape dispenser. You could just pull off as much as you wanted. I'd chew so much my jaw would ache. 

But yeah, no, definitely no seizures. Just the... the blanking out thing.
Have you ever been through something extremely frightening or traumatic?

Traumatic? No, I don't think so. I've never been in a bad accident or a war or anything like that. I mean, standing out on the road with cars flying by can be a little scary sometimes, but you get used to it. You just have to stay alert and keep your eyes moving. That's what they taught us in the certification class. 

The instructor for that class was this really intense guy named Gary. He had this huge, bushy mustache that covered his entire upper lip. It looked like a caterpillar was just resting on his face. I could never grow a mustache, obviously, but sometimes I wonder what it would be like to have facial hair. Like, would it be itchy? My ex-boyfriend had a beard, and he was always scratching it. He used this special beard oil that smelled like cedarwood and vanilla. It was actually a really nice smell. We used to go camping a lot, and the smell of the cedarwood always reminded me of being out in the woods. I love camping, especially in the fall when the leaves are changing colors. The reds and oranges are just so vibrant. I tried to paint a picture of a forest in the fall once, but I'm not very good at watercolors. They always just bleed together and turn into this muddy brown mess. You have to have a really light touch with watercolors, I think. 

But um... no, nothing extremely frightening or traumatic has ever happened to me. Just a normal life, really.
Have you ever been told you have a neurological illness, like a brain infection, stroke, or tumor?

A brain infection or a tumor? No, nothing like that. I've never had a stroke, either. Physically, my brain is fine. I did get a really terrible headache once, but that was just because I forgot my hat at work. Being a flagger, you're just standing out there baking in the sun for hours, so you really need a good hat. I usually wear this wide-brimmed straw one. It has a little toggle string under the chin so it doesn't blow away when the big semi-trucks go past. 

The wind from those trucks is incredible, honestly. One time a truck went by so fast it actually blew my sunglasses right off my face, and they skittered across the asphalt and got completely scratched up. They were my favorite pair, too. They were polarized, which you really need so it cuts the glare off all the car windshields. It is so hard to find good polarized sunglasses that don't cost an absolute fortune. I ended up having to go to this little kiosk at the mall to get a replacement pair. The mall is always so dead these days, though. Half the stores are just empty and gated up. I remember when the mall used to be the place to go on a Friday night when I was a teenager... you'd get a soft pretzel and just walk around looking at things. I love those pretzels with the big chunks of salt on them, especially if you dip them in that fake yellow cheese. 

But um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, the brain thing. No, no tumors or infections or anything like that.
Do these blank spells ever start when something reminds you of a painful or upsetting event from your past?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I told you I haven't really had any bad or painful events like that, so there's nothing to be reminded of. The blank spells just kind of... happen. Usually when I'm just standing there holding the stop sign. It gets so heavy after a while, you know? The pole is made of this thick aluminum, and your arm just starts to ache right around the shoulder joint. I tried switching arms, but I'm so right-hand dominant that it feels incredibly awkward to hold it with my left. 

My left hand is basically useless. I tried to teach myself to write with my left hand once when I was in college, just as a brain exercise. I read this article that said it builds new neural pathways or something. I bought this really nice fountain pen to practice with. It had blue ink, like a really deep cobalt blue. I love that color. I actually painted my living room that color a few years ago, but it ended up making the room look way too dark because I don't get a lot of natural light in there. My apartment only has windows on the north side, so it's always kind of gloomy. My houseplants hate it. I've killed like three ferns already this year. Ferns are so finicky, they need just the right amount of humidity. 

But yeah, the blank spells don't have anything to do with upsetting memories or anything. They just happen out of nowhere.
Have you started any new medicines or drugs around the time these blank spells began?

New medicines? No, I haven't started anything new. I don't really like taking a lot of pills anyway. Even when I get a cold, I try to just drink a lot of tea. Peppermint tea is my favorite. It really clears out your sinuses, you know? I buy it in bulk from this little co-op down the street from my apartment. They have these huge glass jars filled with all kinds of loose leaf teas and herbs. It smells amazing in there, like dried flowers and spices. 

The woman who runs the co-op is so nice, she always gives me a little extra scoop of the peppermint. She has these really beautiful silver rings on every single finger. I always wonder how she manages to do anything with all those rings on. I feel like they would get caught on everything. I used to wear a ring on my thumb when I was in my twenties, but I lost it at a concert. It was a general admission show, and everybody was just packed in so tight. The band was okay, but the bass was so loud it made my teeth rattle. I hate when the bass is that loud, it just vibrates right through your chest cavity. 

But um, no, no new drugs or medicines or anything like that. Just the same old me.
During these blank spells, do you ever feel detached from yourself or like the world around you isn’t real?

Detached? Like things aren't real? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, the world is definitely real. The pavement gets so hot you can literally see the heat waves coming off it, making everything look all wavy and distorted. It's like looking through a funhouse mirror. 

I went to a funhouse once at the state fair when I was a kid. They had this whole hall of mirrors where you looked super tall and skinny, and then the next one made you look short and round like a beach ball. The fair is always so crowded, though. You can barely walk without bumping into someone eating a giant turkey leg. I don't understand how people can eat those things while walking around. They're so messy, and the grease gets everywhere. I prefer cotton candy. The blue kind, not the pink. It just tastes better, even though I know it's probably just the same sugar with different food coloring. I read once that red food dye is made from crushed up beetles. Isn't that disgusting? I try to check the labels on everything now, but the print is always so tiny. I should probably get reading glasses, but I feel like I'm too young for that. My mom started wearing reading glasses when she was forty, and she had them attached to this sparkly beaded chain around her neck so she wouldn't lose them. 

But no, I don't feel detached or anything during the blank spells. I'm just... blank.
Have you ever had an EEG or brain scan for these blank spells?

An EEG? No, I've never had any kind of brain scan or anything like that. I've actually never even been in a hospital, except for when my sister had her baby. She had a little girl, Emily. She's five now, and she is just a handful. She has this curly hair that is impossible to brush. My sister buys all these expensive detangling sprays, but I swear none of them work. They just smell like artificial green apples. 

I actually really hate artificial fruit smells. Like those car air fresheners shaped like little trees? The cherry one gives me an instant headache. My ex-boyfriend used to have one of those in his truck, and I made him throw it out the window one time when we were driving on the highway. I know that's littering, and I felt bad about it later, but the smell was just so overwhelming. His truck was always a mess anyway, fast food wrappers everywhere. He used to eat those spicy chicken sandwiches from the drive-thru like every other day. I don't know how his stomach handled it. Spicy food always gives me terrible heartburn. I have to sleep propped up on two pillows if I even look at a jalapeño. 

But um, no, no brain scans or EEGs for the blank spells. Nobody's ever suggested that before.
During one of these blank spells, has anyone ever told you that you stare off into space?

Stare off into space? I mean, I guess so. I came in because my mind just keeps going completely blank at the worst possible times. Like, I'll be at work—I'm a crossing guard, well, a flagger really, for the construction sites—and I'll look down at the road-closure forms or even just my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I cannot remember the steps I've done for years. It's just... gone. Like someone wiped a chalkboard clean. 

Chalkboards always remind me of elementary school. My third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she used to make us go outside and clap the erasers against the brick wall of the school to get the dust out. We'd be covered in this fine white powder by the time recess was over. It was so bad for our lungs, probably. I read an article once about how much dust we breathe in every day, mostly just dead skin cells. It's horrifying when you really think about it. I bought one of those fancy HEPA air purifiers for my apartment, but the filter replacement costs are just ridiculous. They get you on the refills, you know? It's like printers and ink cartridges. I haven't printed anything in years because the ink dried up and it costs more to buy new ink than to just buy a whole new printer. It's so wasteful. 

But yeah, I don't know if I'm staring into space, exactly, it's just that my mind goes completely blank and I forget what I'm supposed to be doing with the paddle.
Have these blank spells ever happened while you were asleep or just waking up?

While I'm asleep? I'm not really sure how I would know if my mind goes blank while I'm sleeping. I mean, you're unconscious, right? So you wouldn't know. I guess I don't really remember my dreams most of the time anyway. Sometimes I'll wake up and know I had a bad dream, but I can't remember any of the details. Just this lingering feeling of dread, like I forgot to do something really important. 

I hate that feeling. It's like when you leave the house and you're halfway down the street and you suddenly panic because you can't remember if you locked the front door or turned off the stove. I do that with my curling iron all the time. I'll actually turn the car around and drive all the way back home just to check, and it's always unplugged. I should really just start taking a picture of the unplugged cord on my phone before I leave, but then my camera roll would just be hundreds of pictures of a curling iron on a bathroom counter. My phone is already out of storage space anyway. It keeps giving me that annoying pop-up message saying I need to manage my storage, but I don't want to delete any of my pictures. I have all these photos from a trip I took to the Grand Canyon like ten years ago. It's so beautiful there, but the lack of guardrails is terrifying. You just walk right up to the edge and look down. I felt dizzy just standing there. 

But um, no, I haven't noticed them happening when I'm waking up or anything. Just mostly when I'm awake and trying to do things.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are discrete episodes of elevated or unusually energetic mood suggestive of bipolar disorder, which would best distinguish it from ADHD, anxiety, dissociative symptoms, or other cognitive causes.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized or high compared with your normal self?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about manic or hypomanic symptoms (feeling unusually energized or high). There is no symptom in my profile related to mania or hypomania.

patient.answer:
Energized? No... no, I don't think so. Honestly, most of the time I just feel incredibly heavy. Like I'm walking through wet cement. I do try to drink coffee to get some kind of energy for my shifts, though. There's this little drive-thru espresso hut right by the intersection where I'm flagging this week, and the girl working there makes the best mochas. She actually brings her dog to work, this little terrier mix, and it just sits on the counter by the window. 

I always worry about the dog, honestly, because of all the cars idling right there in line. The exhaust can't be good for its little lungs. I read an article once about air quality and how it affects pets faster than humans because they breathe faster... or maybe it's because they're closer to the ground? I can't remember. My mom used to have a dog that had asthma, and they had to give it an inhaler, which just seems so strange to look at. 

But anyway... no. I never really get those big bursts of energy or feel high like you're saying. I'm usually just tired.

inference.note: Ruled against F31.9 this turn: patient denies periods of elevated/expansive energy or feeling high, and instead reports chronic tiredness. Persistent distractibility, tangentiality, and mind going blank still support ADHD vs other cognitive/anxiety-related causes.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the attention lapses and tangentiality began in childhood, which would strongly support ADHD over anxiety, dissociative symptoms, or an organic cognitive disorder.
doctor.question: When you were a child in school, did you often have trouble paying attention?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about childhood attention problems, which screens for ADHD. My symptom profile only covers current diminished thinking and concentration (S031), not childhood attention issues.

patient.answer:
Trouble paying attention in school? I... I don't really remember having a problem with it. I was pretty quiet, mostly. I liked reading. I remember reading this one book about a girl who lived in a windmill, and she had to figure out how to grind the flour herself after her parents left. It was so detailed about the gears and the stones. I actually tried to build a little model windmill out of popsicle sticks and rubber bands for a science project after that. My dad helped me glue the base together because the glue gun was so hot. He used to keep all his tools in these old metal coffee cans in the garage, the kind that smelled like stale coffee and motor oil. He had this whole system for sorting the nails by size, but then my brother knocked one over once and they just went everywhere. It took us hours to pick them all up out of the sawdust on the floor. 

But no, I don't think I had trouble paying attention. I just kind of kept my head down and did my work.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the blanking-out episodes involve losing awareness of time, which would help distinguish a neurological/cognitive cause from anxiety or ADHD.
doctor.question: When your mind goes blank, do you lose track of time?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about losing track of time, which is a screening question for dissociation or absence seizures. This specific symptom is not covered in the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Lose track of time? Um... yeah, I guess I do. It's like... I'll look at the clock on my phone, and it's 10:15, and then I blink, and my supervisor is tapping me on the shoulder to tell me it's time for my lunch break at noon. My phone actually has this really annoying crack right across the screen, right where the time is. I dropped it last week when I was trying to get my keys out of my pocket. My keychain is so heavy because I have all these little charms on it. There's a little Eiffel Tower from when my aunt went to Paris, and this plastic dinosaur that glows in the dark. I think it's a Stegosaurus, the one with the plates on its back. Did you know they think those plates were actually for regulating their body temperature, not just for defense? I read that in a waiting room magazine once. It's fascinating how much we've learned about dinosaurs just from fossils. They even found one recently that had preserved feathers, which completely changes how you picture them. It makes them seem more like giant, scary birds. 

But, um... yeah, the time just kind of vanishes when my head gets empty like that. I just don't know where it goes.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the blank spells involve impaired awareness suggestive of a dissociative or organic episode rather than primary anxiety or ADHD.
doctor.question: During these blank spells, are you aware of what’s happening around you?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my mind keeps going blank at the worst times, like I will look at the road-closure forms or the stop-slow paddle and suddenly cannot remember the steps I have done for years.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking a follow-up question about the 'blank spells' to further understand the patient's diminished ability to think or concentrate.

patient.answer:
Aware? I... I don't think so. That's actually why I came in, to be honest. It's getting really bad at work. I'll be standing there, and I'll look down at the road-closure forms I have to sign, or even just holding my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just... I cannot remember the steps. And I've done this job for years. But my mind just goes completely blank at the worst possible times. 

Like the other day, I was standing by the barricades, and they're those big orange plastic ones, you know? The ones you can fill with water or sand so they don't blow over. The crew usually fills them with water from the hydrant, which always makes me nervous because the water pressure from those things is incredible. I saw a video once where a fire hydrant broke and the water shot up higher than a three-story building. It completely flooded the street in like five minutes. Water damage is so hard to fix, too. My sister had a pipe burst in her basement last winter, and it ruined all her old photo albums. She had these beautiful leather-bound albums from our grandparents' wedding, and they just got completely soaked and warped. She tried to dry them out with a hair dryer, but the pages all stuck together. It was really heartbreaking.

But... yeah, when the blankness happens, I'm just gone. I don't know what's happening around me at all until I snap out of it and realize I don't know what I'm supposed to be doing with the paddle.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the blank spells involve amnesia for the episode, which best distinguishes dissociative episodes from anxiety or ADHD at this point.
doctor.question: After one of these blank spells ends, can you remember what happened during it?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my mind keeps going blank at the worst times, like I will look at the road-closure forms or the stop-slow paddle and suddenly cannot remember the steps I have done for years.
target_item.reason: The doctor is continuing to ask about the 'blank spells' which represent the patient's diminished ability to think or concentrate.

patient.answer:
Remember what happened? No, not really. It's just a blank. Like I was saying, that's the whole reason I'm here. It's just so terrifying to be holding the stop-slow paddle, or staring at those road-closure forms, and I just completely forget the steps. Things I've done for years. It's like someone just hit erase. 

You know, those forms are always printed on this really cheap, thin paper that tears if you even look at it wrong. The ink smears, too, especially when it rains. We have to use these special waterproof clipboards, the ones that have a little plastic cover that folds down over the paper. My supervisor, Dave, he lost his clipboard last month and had to use a regular one during a downpour. The forms practically dissolved. Dave is always losing things, though. He lost his favorite sunglasses in a porta-potty once. He was so mad because they were those expensive polarized ones that cut the glare off the windshields. Glare can be really dangerous out on the road, especially right at sunrise or sunset. The light hits the asphalt and it just blinds you. 

But yeah, I don't remember anything from when it happens. Just... gone. And then I'm standing there holding the paddle like an idiot.

inference.note: Episodes involve unawareness of surroundings, lost time, and complete amnesia for the spell, which argues against primary inattention/ADHD (F90.0) and makes an organic dissociative/nonepileptic phenomenon more likely; kept anxiety as a possible contributor but less favored.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the episodes are triggered by psychological stress or trauma, which would help distinguish dissociative symptoms from an anxiety disorder or another medical cause.
doctor.question: Do these blank spells tend to happen when you’re under emotional stress?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my mind keeps going blank at the worst times, like I will look at the road-closure forms or the stop-slow paddle and suddenly cannot remember the steps I have done for years.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the triggers for the patient's 'blank spells', which relates to the diminished ability to think or concentrate.

patient.answer:
Emotional stress? I mean... maybe? I'm not really sure if it's stress causing it, but like I said, it just happens at the absolute worst times. I'll just be standing there, looking at the road-closure forms or holding my stop-slow paddle, and my mind just completely empties out. I suddenly cannot remember the steps for things I've done for years. It's so frustrating. 

Speaking of those road-closure forms, they changed the font on them recently. It used to be Arial, I think, but now it's something with those little feet on the letters... serifs, right? It makes it look so much more formal, almost like a legal document you'd get from a lawyer. My cousin is a lawyer, actually. She works in corporate law downtown. She has this amazing office on the thirtieth floor with floor-to-ceiling windows. You can see the whole city from up there. She says it's terrifying during thunderstorms, though, because the building actually sways a little bit in the wind. I don't think I could handle that. I get motion sickness just riding in the backseat of a car. I have to chew ginger gum whenever I take a cab. Ginger is supposed to be really good for your digestion, too. I buy these little crystallized ginger pieces from the health food store, but they're so spicy sometimes they make my eyes water. 

But, um... yeah, my mind just goes blank. I don't know if it's stress, but it's why I'm here. I just look at the paddle and I don't know what to do with it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the episodes are linked to a neurological cause such as seizures by checking for involuntary movements during the blank spells.
doctor.question: Has anyone ever told you that you shake or have jerking movements during one of these blank spells?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about shaking or jerking movements (potential seizure activity) during the blank spells, which is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Shake or jerk? No, no one's ever said anything like that to me. I think I just stand there, completely still. Like a statue. Which is why I'm so worried about work, because if I'm just standing there frozen with the stop-slow paddle, someone could get hurt. I just... I forget the steps. 

I did see a statue once that looked incredibly real. It was one of those living statue street performers down by the harbor. He was painted completely bronze, head to toe, and he stood on this little milk crate for hours without blinking. I don't know how they do that without getting muscle cramps. I get a charley horse in my calf almost every night. My doctor told me to eat more bananas for the potassium, but I really can't stand the texture of bananas. They're just so mushy. I prefer apples, especially the Honeycrisp ones when they're in season. They're so expensive, though. I saw them for almost four dollars a pound at the grocery store last week. The prices of everything are just going up so fast. A carton of eggs is ridiculous now. 

But no, nobody has ever told me I shake or anything. I just... freeze up and my mind goes totally blank.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the blank spells are preceded by intense fear or panic, which would help distinguish an anxiety-related cause from dissociative episodes or another medical condition.
doctor.question: Right before one of these blank spells starts, do you suddenly feel a wave of intense fear or panic?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of panic attacks (intense fear or panic) preceding the blank spells, which is not covered by my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Fear or panic? Um... no, I don't think so. I don't feel anything coming on. It's just... one second I'm there, holding the paddle or looking at the forms, and the next second it's just blank. I don't get any kind of warning like that. 

Speaking of warnings, though, we have these new early warning signs for the work zones. They have these really bright, flashing LED lights on them now. They're supposed to be solar-powered, which is great for the environment, you know? I try to do my part, I recycle all my plastics and cardboard. Although, the recycling rules in my neighborhood keep changing. One week you can put glass in the blue bin, the next week you have to take it to a special drop-off center. The drop-off center is right next to this amazing little bakery, though. They make these blueberry scones that are just incredible. They put a lemon glaze on top that perfectly balances out the sweetness. I tried to bake scones at home once, but they turned out hard as rocks. I think my baking powder was expired. You really have to check the expiration dates on things. I drank some milk once that was a week past the date, and my stomach was upset for two whole days. 

But no, I don't feel any panic or fear right before it happens. It just... happens, and then I'm standing there, totally lost.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the episodes involve loss of consciousness with automatisms or post-event confusion suggestive of a neurological seizure disorder rather than dissociative or anxiety-related episodes.
doctor.question: Has anyone ever seen you do repetitive movements, like lip smacking or picking at things, during one of these blank spells?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about automatisms (repetitive movements like lip smacking or picking at things) during the blank spells, which suggests an inquiry into possible seizure activity. My symptom profile does not include symptoms related to seizures or automatisms.

patient.answer:
Lip smacking? No, I don't think so. None of the other flaggers have ever mentioned me doing anything weird like that. Although, my lips do get incredibly chapped out there on the road with all the wind and the dust from the construction. I have to carry this special beeswax lip balm in my safety vest pocket all the time. It has peppermint in it, which is supposed to be really soothing. Peppermint is great for headaches, too, you know. My aunt used to grow real peppermint in her garden. She had this massive garden in her backyard with all these wooden raised beds. She grew tomatoes that were the size of softballs, I swear. We used to make fresh salsa every single summer. I love a good salsa, but it absolutely has to have cilantro in it. Some people think cilantro tastes like soap, which I read somewhere is actually a genetic thing. I think genetics are so fascinating. Like how my sister and I both have the exact same freckle on our left wrist, right over the vein. 

But, um... what was it? Picking at things? No. Nobody has ever said I do anything like that when my mind empties out. I really think I just stand there frozen.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the episodes are associated with a history of neurological insult, which would support an organic mental disorder over dissociative or anxiety-related causes.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a head injury?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a history of head injury to rule out organic causes for the blank spells, which is not covered by any of the psychiatric symptom profiles provided.

patient.answer:
A head injury? No, I've never hit my head or been knocked out or anything like that. I've always been pretty careful. Even when I was a kid, I was the one who wouldn't ride my bike without a helmet. My mom bought me this bright pink helmet with little white stars on it. It was so ugly, but she made me wear it. 

I see kids riding around now without helmets all the time, and it just makes me so nervous. Especially with the way people drive these days. People are always looking at their phones while they're driving. Just yesterday, I was holding the stop sign, and this guy in a silver sedan drove right past me because he was texting. He didn't even look up! I had to blow my whistle so hard I thought I was going to burst an eardrum. Whistles are surprisingly loud when you blow them with all your might. I actually have a special whistle that's designed to cut through the noise of heavy machinery. It's made of this lightweight titanium, so it doesn't weigh down my lanyard. Lanyards can really chafe your neck if you wear them all day in the heat. I tried wrapping mine in a bit of felt, but then it just absorbed all my sweat and got really gross. 

But no, I've never had a concussion or hurt my head. My head is totally fine, except for... well, the blank spells.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a history of seizures, which would strongly support an organic cause over dissociative or anxiety-related episodes.
doctor.question: Have you ever been told that you have seizures or epilepsy?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a history of seizures or epilepsy to rule out neurological causes for the blank spells, which is not covered by any of my symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
Seizures? No, nobody's ever told me that. I've never had a seizure or epilepsy or anything. My health has always been pretty normal, honestly. Except for my allergies, I guess. I have terrible seasonal allergies, especially in the spring when all the pollen is out. The oak trees are the worst for me. There's this massive oak tree right outside my bedroom window, and it just dumps yellow dust all over my car every April. I have to run it through the car wash like twice a week just to see out the windshield. The car wash I go to has those really cool colorful foam soaps, you know? Like bright pink and blue. It smells like bubblegum. I used to love bubblegum when I was little, especially the kind that came in a long tape dispenser. You could just pull off as much as you wanted. I'd chew so much my jaw would ache. 

But yeah, no, definitely no seizures. Just the... the blanking out thing.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the episodes are linked to dissociative triggers by assessing a history of severe psychological trauma.
doctor.question: Have you ever been through something extremely frightening or traumatic?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a history of extremely frightening or traumatic events (screening for PTSD or trauma). My symptom profile does not include a specific item for trauma history.

patient.answer:
Traumatic? No, I don't think so. I've never been in a bad accident or a war or anything like that. I mean, standing out on the road with cars flying by can be a little scary sometimes, but you get used to it. You just have to stay alert and keep your eyes moving. That's what they taught us in the certification class. 

The instructor for that class was this really intense guy named Gary. He had this huge, bushy mustache that covered his entire upper lip. It looked like a caterpillar was just resting on his face. I could never grow a mustache, obviously, but sometimes I wonder what it would be like to have facial hair. Like, would it be itchy? My ex-boyfriend had a beard, and he was always scratching it. He used this special beard oil that smelled like cedarwood and vanilla. It was actually a really nice smell. We used to go camping a lot, and the smell of the cedarwood always reminded me of being out in the woods. I love camping, especially in the fall when the leaves are changing colors. The reds and oranges are just so vibrant. I tried to paint a picture of a forest in the fall once, but I'm not very good at watercolors. They always just bleed together and turn into this muddy brown mess. You have to have a really light touch with watercolors, I think. 

But um... no, nothing extremely frightening or traumatic has ever happened to me. Just a normal life, really.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the episodes are linked to a medical or neurologic condition by checking for a history of serious medical illness affecting the brain.
doctor.question: Have you ever been told you have a neurological illness, like a brain infection, stroke, or tumor?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about neurological illnesses such as brain infections, strokes, or tumors to rule out general medical conditions. My symptom profile does not contain an item related to neurological illnesses.

patient.answer:
A brain infection or a tumor? No, nothing like that. I've never had a stroke, either. Physically, my brain is fine. I did get a really terrible headache once, but that was just because I forgot my hat at work. Being a flagger, you're just standing out there baking in the sun for hours, so you really need a good hat. I usually wear this wide-brimmed straw one. It has a little toggle string under the chin so it doesn't blow away when the big semi-trucks go past. 

The wind from those trucks is incredible, honestly. One time a truck went by so fast it actually blew my sunglasses right off my face, and they skittered across the asphalt and got completely scratched up. They were my favorite pair, too. They were polarized, which you really need so it cuts the glare off all the car windshields. It is so hard to find good polarized sunglasses that don't cost an absolute fortune. I ended up having to go to this little kiosk at the mall to get a replacement pair. The mall is always so dead these days, though. Half the stores are just empty and gated up. I remember when the mall used to be the place to go on a Friday night when I was a teenager... you'd get a soft pretzel and just walk around looking at things. I love those pretzels with the big chunks of salt on them, especially if you dip them in that fake yellow cheese. 

But um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, the brain thing. No, no tumors or infections or anything like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the blank spells are triggered by reminders of past trauma, which would support a dissociative disorder over anxiety or an organic mental disorder.
doctor.question: Do these blank spells ever start when something reminds you of a painful or upsetting event from your past?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the blank spells are triggered by reminders of a painful or upsetting event (trauma triggers/PTSD symptoms), which is not covered by my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, I don't think so. I mean, I told you I haven't really had any bad or painful events like that, so there's nothing to be reminded of. The blank spells just kind of... happen. Usually when I'm just standing there holding the stop sign. It gets so heavy after a while, you know? The pole is made of this thick aluminum, and your arm just starts to ache right around the shoulder joint. I tried switching arms, but I'm so right-hand dominant that it feels incredibly awkward to hold it with my left. 

My left hand is basically useless. I tried to teach myself to write with my left hand once when I was in college, just as a brain exercise. I read this article that said it builds new neural pathways or something. I bought this really nice fountain pen to practice with. It had blue ink, like a really deep cobalt blue. I love that color. I actually painted my living room that color a few years ago, but it ended up making the room look way too dark because I don't get a lot of natural light in there. My apartment only has windows on the north side, so it's always kind of gloomy. My houseplants hate it. I've killed like three ferns already this year. Ferns are so finicky, they need just the right amount of humidity. 

But yeah, the blank spells don't have anything to do with upsetting memories or anything. They just happen out of nowhere.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is an underlying medical or substance cause for the blank spells, which best separates dissociative symptoms from anxiety and other specified mental disorder due to another medical condition.
doctor.question: Have you started any new medicines or drugs around the time these blank spells began?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the use of new medicines or drugs to rule out substance-induced cognitive issues, which is not covered by any of the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
New medicines? No, I haven't started anything new. I don't really like taking a lot of pills anyway. Even when I get a cold, I try to just drink a lot of tea. Peppermint tea is my favorite. It really clears out your sinuses, you know? I buy it in bulk from this little co-op down the street from my apartment. They have these huge glass jars filled with all kinds of loose leaf teas and herbs. It smells amazing in there, like dried flowers and spices. 

The woman who runs the co-op is so nice, she always gives me a little extra scoop of the peppermint. She has these really beautiful silver rings on every single finger. I always wonder how she manages to do anything with all those rings on. I feel like they would get caught on everything. I used to wear a ring on my thumb when I was in my twenties, but I lost it at a concert. It was a general admission show, and everybody was just packed in so tight. The band was okay, but the bass was so loud it made my teeth rattle. I hate when the bass is that loud, it just vibrates right through your chest cavity. 

But um, no, no new drugs or medicines or anything like that. Just the same old me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the episodes are accompanied by depersonalization or derealization, which would help distinguish a dissociative disorder from anxiety or another mental disorder due to a medical condition.
doctor.question: During these blank spells, do you ever feel detached from yourself or like the world around you isn’t real?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of depersonalization or derealization (feeling detached from oneself or the world not feeling real) during the blank spells. These symptoms are not covered by any of the items in the provided symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Detached? Like things aren't real? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, the world is definitely real. The pavement gets so hot you can literally see the heat waves coming off it, making everything look all wavy and distorted. It's like looking through a funhouse mirror. 

I went to a funhouse once at the state fair when I was a kid. They had this whole hall of mirrors where you looked super tall and skinny, and then the next one made you look short and round like a beach ball. The fair is always so crowded, though. You can barely walk without bumping into someone eating a giant turkey leg. I don't understand how people can eat those things while walking around. They're so messy, and the grease gets everywhere. I prefer cotton candy. The blue kind, not the pink. It just tastes better, even though I know it's probably just the same sugar with different food coloring. I read once that red food dye is made from crushed up beetles. Isn't that disgusting? I try to check the labels on everything now, but the print is always so tiny. I should probably get reading glasses, but I feel like I'm too young for that. My mom started wearing reading glasses when she was forty, and she had them attached to this sparkly beaded chain around her neck so she wouldn't lose them. 

But no, I don't feel detached or anything during the blank spells. I'm just... blank.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the episodes are associated with clear medical findings suggestive of a neurological cause rather than anxiety or dissociative symptoms.
doctor.question: Have you ever had an EEG or brain scan for these blank spells?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I have had an EEG or brain scan for the blank spells, which is related to medical workup and excluding neurological causes. There is no specific symptom profile item for medical workups like EEGs or brain scans.

patient.answer:
An EEG? No, I've never had any kind of brain scan or anything like that. I've actually never even been in a hospital, except for when my sister had her baby. She had a little girl, Emily. She's five now, and she is just a handful. She has this curly hair that is impossible to brush. My sister buys all these expensive detangling sprays, but I swear none of them work. They just smell like artificial green apples. 

I actually really hate artificial fruit smells. Like those car air fresheners shaped like little trees? The cherry one gives me an instant headache. My ex-boyfriend used to have one of those in his truck, and I made him throw it out the window one time when we were driving on the highway. I know that's littering, and I felt bad about it later, but the smell was just so overwhelming. His truck was always a mess anyway, fast food wrappers everywhere. He used to eat those spicy chicken sandwiches from the drive-thru like every other day. I don't know how his stomach handled it. Spicy food always gives me terrible heartburn. I have to sleep propped up on two pillows if I even look at a jalapeño. 

But um, no, no brain scans or EEGs for the blank spells. Nobody's ever suggested that before.

doctor.intent: Determine whether these episodes have any observable automatisms or altered behavior that would suggest an organic seizure disorder rather than dissociative blank spells or anxiety.
doctor.question: During one of these blank spells, has anyone ever told you that you stare off into space?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my mind keeps going blank at the worst times, like I will look at the road-closure forms or the stop-slow paddle and suddenly cannot remember the steps I have done for years.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking for more details about my 'blank spells', which are a manifestation of my diminished ability to think or concentrate.

patient.answer:
Stare off into space? I mean, I guess so. I came in because my mind just keeps going completely blank at the worst possible times. Like, I'll be at work—I'm a crossing guard, well, a flagger really, for the construction sites—and I'll look down at the road-closure forms or even just my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I cannot remember the steps I've done for years. It's just... gone. Like someone wiped a chalkboard clean. 

Chalkboards always remind me of elementary school. My third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she used to make us go outside and clap the erasers against the brick wall of the school to get the dust out. We'd be covered in this fine white powder by the time recess was over. It was so bad for our lungs, probably. I read an article once about how much dust we breathe in every day, mostly just dead skin cells. It's horrifying when you really think about it. I bought one of those fancy HEPA air purifiers for my apartment, but the filter replacement costs are just ridiculous. They get you on the refills, you know? It's like printers and ink cartridges. I haven't printed anything in years because the ink dried up and it costs more to buy new ink than to just buy a whole new printer. It's so wasteful. 

But yeah, I don't know if I'm staring into space, exactly, it's just that my mind goes completely blank and I forget what I'm supposed to be doing with the paddle.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the episodes are due to an underlying neurological condition rather than dissociative or anxiety-related causes by asking about episodes occurring during sleep.
doctor.question: Have these blank spells ever happened while you were asleep or just waking up?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the blank spells occur while asleep or just waking up, which is a specific detail about the episodes not covered in the symptom profile.

patient.answer:
While I'm asleep? I'm not really sure how I would know if my mind goes blank while I'm sleeping. I mean, you're unconscious, right? So you wouldn't know. I guess I don't really remember my dreams most of the time anyway. Sometimes I'll wake up and know I had a bad dream, but I can't remember any of the details. Just this lingering feeling of dread, like I forgot to do something really important. 

I hate that feeling. It's like when you leave the house and you're halfway down the street and you suddenly panic because you can't remember if you locked the front door or turned off the stove. I do that with my curling iron all the time. I'll actually turn the car around and drive all the way back home just to check, and it's always unplugged. I should really just start taking a picture of the unplugged cord on my phone before I leave, but then my camera roll would just be hundreds of pictures of a curling iron on a bathroom counter. My phone is already out of storage space anyway. It keeps giving me that annoying pop-up message saying I need to manage my storage, but I don't want to delete any of my pictures. I have all these photos from a trip I took to the Grand Canyon like ten years ago. It's so beautiful there, but the lack of guardrails is terrifying. You just walk right up to the edge and look down. I felt dizzy just standing there. 

But um, no, I haven't noticed them happening when I'm waking up or anything. Just mostly when I'm awake and trying to do things.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent episodes of abrupt blank staring with loss of awareness, loss of time, and post-episode amnesia during wakefulness, without panic, depersonalization, trauma linkage, or clear psychosocial precipitants. This pattern is more consistent with a neurological-type cognitive disturbance than with anxiety disorder or dissociative disorder. Among the provided options, other specified mental disorders due to known physiological condition is the best fit, while dissociative disorder remains a differential pending neurological evaluation.
